exercise1.prompt: Arrays of different shapes can still meet, under one clear rule.

hiddenCases.name: one value is its own mean
the subtraction reaches the whole array at once

exercise1.hint: values - values.mean() does the whole thing. np.round then rounds the array, and list() turns it back into plain numbers.

choices: Stretching a smaller shape so it can meet a larger one
questions.explain: A single number meeting an array is the simplest case, and the rule extends to a row meeting a table.

questions.prompt: What does prices - prices.mean() give you?
choices: An array of distances from the average
questions.explain: The mean is one number broadcast across every element, so each result says how far that price sits from the middle.

questions.prompt: Two arrays of the same length are added. What happens?
choices: They are joined end to end
They are added position by position
questions.explain: Elementwise, unlike lists, where + concatenates. Getting these two the wrong way round is the most common early mistake.
